role: researcher/author of BART energy study for Caltrans
stance_basis: cited as a data source for construction energy estimates, with no personal position expressed
summary: Timothy J. Healy is referenced solely as the author of a 1973 Caltrans study on BART energy requirements, which is used to estimate that construction of grade-separated rapid transit alternatives could require up to 55% of propulsion energy. His work is cited as a data input rather than as an advocacy position, and the document notes his results have never been verified nor substantiated. He does not express any personal stance on the project.
complaint_summary: Healy's 1973 Caltrans study on BART energy requirements is cited to estimate that construction of grade-separated rapid transit alternatives (I-VI) could require as much as 55% of propulsion energy, though the document notes these results are unverified and purely hypothetical.
summary_quote: Based upon energy estimates for BART construction made by Timothy J. Healy, "Energy Requirements of the BART System", developed for Caltrans 1973, construction of the grade-separated rapid transit alternatives (I-VI) could require as much as 55 percent of the propulsion energy.
